result: Embryonic activation of Pik3caH1047R mutation in GFAP-cre mice causes stereotypic gyrification of the hippocampus and neocortex with 100% penetrance, meeting criteria for bona fide cortical folding, and recapitulates human PI3K-related developmental hydrocephalus.
evaluation: Claims C1-C11 collectively demonstrate that the Pik3caH1047R mutation causes reproducible gyrification with complete penetrance (n>50), supported by extensive histological evidence (Figures 1, 1-supplements), comparison to established gyrification criteria (Borrell 2018), and replication in different cre lines (Emx1-cre). The phenotype includes ventriculomegaly evident from E14.5 and meets all criteria for bona fide gyrification.

result: Pik3caH1047R mutants maintain normal hippocampal patterning and neuronal fate specification despite gyrification primarily restricted to CA1 and increased CA field/dentate gyrus lengths.
evaluation: Claims C12-C14 and C22 show that despite dramatic morphological changes, hippocampal subdivisions (CA1-4, DG) remain properly patterned (Figure 1g-l), gyrification is localized to CA1, and birth-dating analysis confirms normal neuronal fate specification (Figure 2-supplement 1a-c). Quantitative measurements demonstrate significant increases in CA1 and DG lengths with appropriate statistical analysis.

result: Pik3caH1047R mutants replicate the canonical gyrification sequence seen in naturally gyrencephalic mammals, with temporal progression from increased apical progenitors and proliferation at E14.5 to expansion of secondary progenitors (Tbr2+ IPs) at E16.5 and enhanced neuronal differentiation.
evaluation: Claims C16-C21 demonstrate a coordinated developmental sequence with appropriate temporal controls (E14.5 vs E16.5). Statistical analyses support significantly longer ventricular linings (p=0.0028, p<0.0001), increased proliferation at E14.5 (p<0.05), temporal shifts in Sox2+ and Tbr2+ progenitor populations (p<0.05, p<0.01), and increased neuronal differentiation at E16.5 (Figure 2). The sequence matches that described in naturally gyrencephalic species.

result: Disrupted Nestin+/GFAP+ radial glial scaffold is observed throughout embryogenesis starting at E14.5 in Pik3caH1047R mutants.
evaluation: Claim C23 is supported by immunohistochemical data (Figure 2-supplement 1d-i) and consistent with previous reports (Roy et al., 2015). The disruption is evident across multiple developmental stages and represents a key cellular phenotype underlying the gyrification.

result: Pik3ca-driven gyrification has a critical period from E13.5 to E15.5, with a 2-day window sufficient to recapitulate the full stereotypic gyrification pattern, while ventriculomegaly results from mutation induction at any embryonic time point.
evaluation: Claims C24-C29 define distinct temporal requirements through systematic doxycycline manipulation experiments (Figure 3). The data show postnatal induction is ineffective (C24), E0.5 or E13.5 induction produces identical severe phenotypes (C25), a 2-day window (E13.5>E15.5) is sufficient for full gyrification (C27), shorter windows are insufficient (C28), and later induction causes gradual attenuation (C29). Quantitative measurements support these conclusions (Figure 3-supplement 1a).

result: The first morphological sign of gyrification in minimally induced mutants is a medial ripple at E17.5, and ectopic Reelin+ cells are not present in mutant CA1 regions.
evaluation: Claims C30-C31 are supported by temporal analysis of minimally induced mutants (dox E13.5>E15.5) showing the ripple at E17.5 (Figure 3-supplement 1f-n) and immunohistochemical analysis excluding ectopic Reelin at E17.5 and P2 (Figure 2-supplement 1m,n; Figure 3-supplement 1r,v). This rules out one potential mechanism (ectopic Reelin) for the phenotype.

result: Disruption of apical cell adhesion is the earliest detectable abnormality in Pik3caH1047R mutants, with junctional proteins (β-Catenin, N-Cadherin, ZO-1) becoming focally discontinuous and ectopic, leading to unzippered ventricular linings.
evaluation: Claims C32-C34 demonstrate progressive disruption of apical adhesion from subtle changes at E14.5 to gaps/bubbles at E16.5 to complete unzippering postnatally (Figure 4, Figure 4-supplement 1). Multiple junctional proteins show consistent abnormalities with high-resolution confocal imaging. This represents the earliest known substrate for gyrification.

result: Aberrant nuclear localization of Yap is observed in Pik3caH1047R mutants from E14.5 onwards, with significantly increased nYap+ cells particularly at developing gyri, while control mice maintain predominantly cytoplasmic Yap localization.
evaluation: Claims C35-C39 demonstrate altered Yap subcellular localization through immunohistochemistry at multiple stages (E14.5, E16.5, P3) with quantitative analysis showing significantly higher nYap+ cells in mutant sulcus and gyrus (p<0.0001, Figure 5l). The spatial correlation with gyrification zones and temporal progression from E14.5 support a causal role.

result: Verteporfin treatment attenuates gyrification severity and completely rescues ventriculomegaly in 100% of mutant brains, with RNA-seq analysis showing that verteporfin shifts mutant gene expression toward control levels, particularly normalizing PI3K and Hippo-Yap pathway genes.
evaluation: Claims C40-C43 demonstrate therapeutic efficacy through morphological analysis (100% rescue, Figure 6b-g), principal component analysis of RNA-seq data showing gene expression normalization (Figure 6h-i), and gene set enrichment analysis confirming pathway-specific effects (Figure 6-supplement 2). The complete penetrance of ventriculomegaly rescue and partial gyrification attenuation support the mechanistic model.

result: Gene expression profiles of Pik3caH1047R mutant gyri and sulci show considerable overlap with those from naturally gyrencephalic ferret brain.
evaluation: Claim C44 is supported by comparative transcriptomic analysis showing overlap between mouse mutant and ferret gyrification genes (Figure 6-supplement 3a,b). This cross-species validation suggests physiological relevance of the model, though the extent of overlap and functional significance could be further characterized.

result: Verteporfin treatment normalizes apical cell polarity, eliminates ectopic nYap+ cells, restores contiguous junctions, streamlines radial glia, and reduces basal progenitors to near-control levels without affecting apoptosis.
evaluation: Claims C45-C48 demonstrate cellular-level rescue through immunohistochemistry showing normalized ZO-1, Yap, Six3, Vimentin, Nestin, and Tbr2 expression patterns (Figure 7). Quantitative analyses confirm significant normalization of nYap+ and Tbr2+ cell numbers (Figure 7t,u,v). TUNEL assay excludes apoptosis as a mechanism (Figure 7-supplement 2h). The comprehensive cellular characterization supports the mechanistic interpretation.

result: Brief embryonic Pik3ca activation drives subtle changes in apical cell adhesion and Yap translocation, initiating the stereotypic gyrification sequence, and verteporfin treatment rescues these phenotypes, defining apical cell-adhesion as the earliest known substrate for cortical gyrification.
evaluation: Claims C49-C51 synthesize the major findings into a coherent mechanistic model supported by the temporal manipulation experiments (C27-C29), adhesion disruption data (C32-C34), Yap mislocalization (C35-C39), and verteporfin rescue (C40-C48). The conclusion that apical cell-adhesion is the earliest substrate is justified by the E14.5 timing and the comprehensive experimental evidence.

result: PI3K activation during a critical two-day embryonic period disrupts apical junctions and causes Yap translocation leading to gyrification and hydrocephalus, demonstrating that the PI3K/Hippo-Yap pathway is finely tuned to regulate cell adhesion and proliferation to maintain the lissencephalic mouse brain.
evaluation: Claims C61-C64 represent the main conclusions of the study, synthesizing the critical period data (C27), adhesion disruption (C32-C34), Yap mislocalization (C35-C39), and verteporfin rescue (C40-C48). The conclusions are well-supported by the comprehensive experimental evidence, though the precise molecular mechanisms linking PI3K to Yap remain partially characterized.

result: The Pik3caH1047R allele remains tightly dependent on p85 regulation and is functionally not an overexpression allele despite being a strongly activating mutation.
evaluation: Claims C65-C66 are supported by citations to previous biochemical studies (Geering et al., 2007; Zhao and Vogt, 2008; Roy et al., 2015; Gymnopoulos et al., 2007). This characterization is important for interpreting the phenotype as resulting from pathway activation rather than massive overexpression, though direct biochemical validation in this study would strengthen the claim.

result: Exquisite PI3K-dependent regulation of apical cell adhesion is essential for normal mouse brain development, and focal loss of apical integrity correlates with focal Yap translocation from cytoplasm to nucleus at the ventricular lining.
evaluation: Claims C67-C68 are supported by the correlation between adhesion disruption (C32-C34) and Yap mislocalization (C35-C39), the critical period data (C27-C29), and the verteporfin rescue (C40-C48). The correlation is strong, though the claim of causality would be strengthened by additional mechanistic experiments directly manipulating adhesion or Yap independently.

result: Yap is a central regulator of the Hippo pathway with dual cytoplasmic (maintaining cell adhesion) and nuclear (driving proliferation) functions, and PI3K-PDK1 activation promotes nuclear Yap translocation while verteporfin disintegrates the Yap-TEAD complex.
evaluation: Claims C69-C76 establish the mechanistic framework through extensive citations to established literature (Gumbiner and Kim 2014; Park et al. 2016, 2018; Hansen et al. 2015; Lavado et al. 2018; Fan et al. 2013; Liu-Chittenden et al. 2012). These are well-established mechanisms in the field that provide the conceptual basis for the experimental design and interpretation.

result: This is the first study to successfully administer verteporfin intraperitoneally to pregnant mice to suppress nYap function in embryos across the placental barrier, though the gyrification phenotype was not fully rescued, likely due to multiple PI3K downstream outputs beyond Yap.
evaluation: Claims C77-C79 are supported by the experimental data showing partial rescue of gyrification and complete rescue of hydrocephalus (C40). The novelty claim (C77) appears reasonable given the literature search, though the authors acknowledge potential off-target effects. The incomplete rescue (C78) is honestly reported and the interpretation is reasonable given PI3K pathway complexity.

result: Subtle changes in apical adhesion and Yap distribution in early progenitors may initiate gyrification in higher mammals, supported by recent findings that YAP maintains basal progenitors in ferret and human neocortex and that verteporfin reduces basal progenitors in these species.
evaluation: Claims C80-C82 represent speculation (C80 explicitly states "we speculate") supported by convergent findings from Kostic et al. 2019 in ferret and human tissue. While the mouse data are solid and the ferret/human data are supportive, direct testing of this hypothesis in naturally gyrencephalic species would be required for full support. The speculation is reasonable but remains to be definitively proven.

result: Embryonic Pik3caH1047R induction causes ventriculomegaly progressing to hydrocephalus with a longer critical period (ending E17.5) than gyrification (E13.5-E15.5), and verteporfin rescues ventriculomegaly, demonstrating that disrupted apical adhesion and aberrant nYap localization are central to both phenotypes.
evaluation: Claims C87-C91 demonstrate distinct but overlapping temporal requirements for the two phenotypes through systematic temporal manipulation (Figure 3, C26, C29) and show complete rescue of ventriculomegaly with verteporfin (C40, C90). The longer critical period for hydrocephalus compared to gyrification is well-documented, supporting partially separable mechanisms with a common cellular substrate.

result: The normally uniform layer of Vimentin+/Yap+ developing ependymal cells is disrupted at mid-embryonic stages in mutants, with ependymal-fate cells intermingled with progenitors and neurons, and verteporfin reverses this phenotype, demonstrating that early Yap-dependent apical adhesion is required for normal ependymal development during pre-ciliogenesis stages.
evaluation: Claims C95-C98 demonstrate ependymal developmental defects through immunohistochemistry (Figure 5, Figure 6-supplement 1, Figure 7) and show rescue with verteporfin (C97). The conclusion that Yap-dependent adhesion is required during pre-ciliogenesis (C98) is supported by the temporal data and represents a novel finding about ependymal development timing.

result: Altered periventricular cell adhesion caused by dysregulated Hippo-Yap signaling is a common convergent mechanism for both developmental and post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus, as shown by human post-mortem studies, LPA-induced mouse models, and genetic YAP deletion studies.
evaluation: Claims C99-C102 synthesize findings from multiple independent studies (Morales et al. 2012; Jiménez et al. 2014; Guerra et al. 2015; Yung et al. 2015; Park et al. 2016) with the current results to propose a unifying mechanism. The convergence of evidence from different etiologies (genetic, hemorrhagic) and species (mouse, human) strongly supports this conclusion, though it remains correlative across studies.

result: Fine regulation of the Hippo-Yap pathway may represent a new therapeutic approach for pediatric hydrocephalus, as verteporfin effectively crosses the placenta and has minimal effect on normal brain development.
evaluation: Claims C103-C104 are supported by the complete rescue of ventriculomegaly (C40), minimal effects on control littermates (C40, Figure 6-supplement 1), and RNA-seq data showing limited impact on control gene expression (C41). However, this represents a preclinical finding requiring extensive additional validation before clinical translation. The therapeutic potential is promising but preliminary.

result: Disruption of apical surface integrity via enhanced PI3K-Yap signaling alters neurogenesis and initiates gyrification while disrupting ependymal development and causing hydrocephalus, explaining the coincidence of these phenotypes in patients with cortical dysplasia and supporting nuclear Yap as a therapeutic target.
evaluation: Claims C105-C108 represent the main conclusions synthesizing all experimental findings. The conclusions are well-supported by the comprehensive data on gyrification (C1-C29), adhesion disruption (C32-C34), Yap mislocalization (C35-C39), ependymal defects (C95-C98), and therapeutic rescue (C40-C48). The clinical relevance is supported by citations to patient studies (Keppler-Noreuil et al. 2014; Jansen et al. 2015; Roy et al. 2015; Parrini et al. 2016; Furey et al. 2018).
